identity-center.q: Why is creating long-lived IAM users per person a poor fit for large enterprises?
options: Identity sprawl across many accounts becomes unmanageable
identity-center.explain: Repeating users across hundreds of accounts causes identity sprawl; Identity Center centralizes workforce access.

identity-center.q: IAM Identity Center is primarily designed for:
options: Workforce single sign-on across AWS accounts
identity-center.explain: It is AWS’s workforce SSO service for human access to accounts and apps.

identity-center.q: What does SSO stand for in this context?
identity-center.explain: Single Sign-On: one login experience for many apps/accounts.

identity-center.q: A Permission Set in Identity Center is best described as:
options: A reusable bundle of IAM policies assigned to users/groups for accounts
identity-center.explain: Permission sets define what someone can do and are assigned per account.

identity-center.q: AWS Organizations helps enterprises mainly by:
options: Grouping multiple AWS accounts under one organization
identity-center.explain: Organizations manages multi-account structure used with Identity Center.

identity-center.q: Temporary credentials for AWS access are typically issued by:
identity-center.explain: STS issues short-lived credentials after federation/assume-role.

identity-center.q: AssumeRole is used to:
options: Obtain temporary credentials to act under an IAM role
identity-center.explain: Assuming a role returns temporary credentials with that role’s permissions.

identity-center.q: Compared with long-lived access keys, temporary credentials are better because they:
options: Never expire and never need rotation
Expire automatically, reducing risk if leaked
identity-center.explain: Short TTL limits blast radius of credential leaks.

identity-center.q: SAML and OIDC are used in enterprise identity mainly for:
identity-center.explain: They are federation protocols linking corporate IdPs to AWS.

identity-center.q: CLI access with Identity Center typically relies on:
options: SSO login / temporary credentials rather than permanent keys
identity-center.explain: Modern CLI workflows use SSO sessions and temporary creds.

identity-center.q: Identity Center replaces the need for thousands of permanent IAM users primarily by using:
options: Centralized directory + permission sets + temporary access
identity-center.explain: Central identity + temporary access is the enterprise pattern.

identity-center.q: Which is a sign you should move from classic IAM users to Identity Center?
options: You have one laptop and no cloud
You only use free tier once
Many employees and many AWS accounts need managed access
identity-center.explain: Multi-user, multi-account orgs need centralized workforce identity.

identity-center.q: During SSO login, the user ultimately receives access based on:
options: Their assigned permission sets and account memberships
identity-center.explain: Assignments of permission sets to accounts drive access.

identity-center.q: The lesson’s core security theme for workforce access is:
options: Share one IAM user for the whole company
Prefer centralized identity and temporary credentials
identity-center.explain: Centralized SSO + least privilege temporary access is the point.

identity-center.q: AWS Identity Center was formerly commonly known as:
identity-center.explain: The product was rebranded from AWS SSO to IAM Identity Center.

identity-center.q: What should enterprises avoid for day-to-day human access?
options: Long-lived IAM user access keys shared widely
identity-center.explain: Long-lived shared keys are a major risk; use federated temporary access.

identity-center.q: Which statement best matches multi-account access design?
options: Central identity assigns access into accounts via roles/permission sets
One IAM user is created identically in every account by hand forever
identity-center.explain: Central assignment into accounts is the Identity Center model.

identity-center.q: Temporary session credentials typically include:
options: Access key, secret key, and session token (short-lived)
identity-center.explain: STS sessions use key + secret + session token.

identity-center.q: A corporate identity provider (IdP) integrates so that employees:
options: Must create new AWS passwords every hour forever by hand
Use existing company login (e.g. Okta/Azure AD) to reach AWS
identity-center.explain: Federation lets corporate credentials gate AWS access.

identity-center.q: Least privilege with Identity Center means:
options: Everyone is AdministratorAccess in all accounts
Permission sets grant only what each role needs
identity-center.explain: Permission sets should be scoped to needed actions/resources.

identity-center.q: A company has 300 AWS accounts and 4,000 employees. They still create IAM users in each account. What is the best next step?
options: Adopt IAM Identity Center with permission sets across accounts
Put all employees in one EC2 security group
identity-center.explain: Identity Center centralizes workforce access and temporary credentials across accounts.

identity-center.q: An engineer needs CLI access for 2 hours without long-lived keys. Which approach matches the lesson?
options: Use SSO/Identity Center login to obtain temporary credentials
Commit keys in a private repo
Use the root account access key
identity-center.explain: SSO sessions issue temporary STS credentials instead of permanent keys.

identity-center.q: Security wants least privilege for developers in the prod account only. What should they configure?
options: AdministratorAccess on every account for all staff
A permission set with limited policies assigned only to the prod account
identity-center.explain: Permission sets scoped per account enforce least privilege.

identity-center.q: Employees already log into Okta. How should AWS access be designed?
options: Ignore Okta and create local IAM users forever
Share one IAM user named company
Federate the corporate IdP with Identity Center (SAML/OIDC)
identity-center.explain: Federation connects the corporate IdP to AWS SSO/Identity Center.

identity-center.q: A leaked 2-year-old IAM access key was found in GitHub. Which design would have reduced impact?
identity-center.explain: Short-lived credentials expire and limit blast radius.

kms-secrets.q: Encryption primarily protects data by:
options: Making it unreadable without the correct key
Moving it to another region only
kms-secrets.explain: Encryption transforms data so keys are required to decrypt.

kms-secrets.q: Symmetric encryption uses:
options: The same key for encrypt and decrypt
kms-secrets.explain: Symmetric schemes share one secret key for both operations.

kms-secrets.q: Asymmetric encryption uses:
kms-secrets.explain: Public encrypt / private decrypt (or vice versa for signing).

kms-secrets.q: AWS KMS is primarily a service for:
kms-secrets.explain: KMS manages keys and crypto operations.

kms-secrets.q: A Customer Managed Key (CMK) is:
options: A key you create and control policies for in KMS
kms-secrets.explain: CMKs are customer-controlled KMS keys with key policies.

kms-secrets.q: Envelope encryption means:
options: Encrypting data with a data key, then encrypting that data key with a master key
Only using HTTPS for web pages
kms-secrets.explain: Data keys encrypt payloads; KMS protects the data keys.

kms-secrets.q: A data key is typically used to:
kms-secrets.explain: Data keys encrypt large data; KMS focuses on key management.

kms-secrets.q: Secrets Manager is best for:
options: Storing and rotating secrets like DB passwords and API keys
kms-secrets.explain: It stores secrets with optional automatic rotation.

kms-secrets.q: Hardcoding production DB passwords in source code is bad because:
options: Secrets leak via repos, logs, and images
kms-secrets.explain: Secrets in code leak easily; use Secrets Manager/KMS patterns.

kms-secrets.q: Key policies in KMS control:
kms-secrets.explain: Key policies are the primary access control for KMS keys.

kms-secrets.q: AWS managed keys vs customer managed keys:
options: Customer managed keys give more control over policy/rotation/lifecycle
AWS managed keys only work offline
kms-secrets.explain: CMKs provide customer control; AWS managed keys are service-operated.

kms-secrets.q: Rotation of secrets reduces risk by:
options: Limiting how long a leaked secret remains valid
kms-secrets.explain: Regular rotation shortens the usefulness of stolen secrets.

kms-secrets.q: Which pair is the typical split of responsibility?
options: KMS for keys; Secrets Manager for secret values
KMS for DNS; Secrets Manager for VPCs
kms-secrets.explain: KMS = keys/crypto ops; Secrets Manager = secret material lifecycle.

kms-secrets.q: Decrypting with KMS requires:
options: kms:Decrypt (or related) permission on the key
Root password in the client always
kms-secrets.explain: Callers need explicit KMS permissions on the key.

kms-secrets.q: Why is envelope encryption efficient for large files?
options: Bulk data is encrypted locally with data keys; KMS only wraps small keys
kms-secrets.explain: Avoids sending huge payloads to KMS for every byte.

kms-secrets.q: A common anti-pattern is:
kms-secrets.explain: Secrets in git are a classic incident source.

kms-secrets.q: Parameter Store vs Secrets Manager (high level):
options: Secrets Manager focuses on secrets + rotation; Parameter Store is broader config/parameters
kms-secrets.explain: Secrets Manager is specialized for secrets lifecycle; SSM Parameter Store is general config.

kms-secrets.q: Encrypting data at rest means:
options: Data is encrypted while stored on disk/object storage
kms-secrets.explain: At-rest encryption protects stored data; in-transit is separate.

kms-secrets.q: If a CMK is scheduled for deletion, applications that depend on it:
options: Automatically switch to root keys with no impact
Can fail to decrypt until restored/available
kms-secrets.explain: Key deletion/disablement breaks decrypt paths.

kms-secrets.q: Best practice for app access to secrets is:
options: Embed secrets in Docker images as plain text forever
Fetch secrets at runtime with IAM role permissions
kms-secrets.explain: Runtime fetch via roles keeps secrets out of images/code.

kms-secrets.q: An app encrypts multi-GB files. Calling KMS Encrypt on every byte is too slow. What pattern should they use?
options: Envelope encryption: data key for bulk data, KMS wraps the data key
kms-secrets.explain: Envelope encryption keeps bulk crypto local while KMS protects keys.

kms-secrets.q: A database password is hardcoded in a Docker image. What is the correct fix?
options: Make the image public so it's honest
Store the secret in Secrets Manager and fetch at runtime with a task/instance role
Put the password in the AMI name
kms-secrets.explain: Secrets Manager + IAM role avoids secrets in images.

kms-secrets.q: Finance requires customer control of key policy and rotation. Which key type?
options: AWS owned key with no visibility
A password in .env committed to git
kms-secrets.explain: CMKs give customer control of policy and lifecycle.

kms-secrets.q: An IR team finds a secret that may have leaked yesterday. What reduces ongoing risk?
options: Post it in Slack for awareness
Rotate the secret and revoke old versions/credentials
kms-secrets.explain: Rotation invalidates leaked material.

kms-secrets.q: Lambda needs to decrypt a ciphertext blob. What must be true?
options: The execution role needs kms:Decrypt on that key
kms-secrets.explain: KMS enforces key policy + IAM for Decrypt.

options: Call each other synchronously and fail together under load

messaging.q: Asynchronous communication helps by:

messaging.explain: Queues/events decouple timing and availability.

messaging.q: Amazon SQS is primarily a:

messaging.q: A key benefit of SQS is:
messaging.explain: Producers enqueue; consumers process independently.

messaging.q: Standard SQS queues prioritize:
options: High throughput with at-least-once delivery (order not strictly guaranteed)
messaging.explain: Standard = scale; possible duplicates; best-effort ordering.

messaging.q: FIFO SQS queues are chosen when you need:
options: First-in-first-out ordering and exactly-once processing semantics within limits
messaging.explain: FIFO preserves order and deduplication capabilities.

messaging.q: Visibility timeout means:
options: After a consumer receives a message, it is hidden for a period while processing
messaging.explain: Prevents other consumers from getting the same message during processing.

messaging.q: A Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) is used for:
messaging.explain: DLQs capture poison messages after max receives.

messaging.q: Amazon SNS is best described as:
messaging.explain: SNS publishes to many subscribers.

cloudfront.q: Latency on the internet is mainly:
options: Delay for data to travel between client and server
cloudfront.explain: Distance and network hops add latency.

options: Caching content at edge locations closer to users
Forcing one central data center only
cloudfront.explain: Edges serve cached content nearby.
